In Iran, the country's deputy foreign minister says Washington is reviewing Tehran’s proposal to end the war. And in Brazil, Bolsonaro wins Brazil's first round election.

stories.title: Spanish police remove over 3,000 migrants from Ceuta beach camp
stories.summary: Police dismantle a migrant camp on Ceuta’s Trampolín Beach, moving over 3,000 people from tents to a temporary reception centre for processing.

stories.title: FBI arrests woman accused of spying on Taiwanese leader's family in the US

stories.title: Clashes in French cities as students continue to protest over education funding
stories.summary: Students in Marseille and Lille escalate protests over education funding, barricading schools and clashing with police as blockades spread across France.

stories.title: US meeting in Poland excluding France, UK, Baltics risks dividing NATO
stories.summary: US Undersecretary of Defense Elbridge Colby is hosting representatives from five key NATO members in Poland to discuss defence capabilities and the future of the alliance. Critics warn the exclusion of some Allies risks creating a “toxic” divide.

stories.title: FlyDubai co-pilot planned to crash aircraft into Tel Aviv airport
stories.summary: The FlyDubai co-pilot behind the hijacking attempt wanted to crash the jet into Ben Gurion Airport and previously flew the sensitive Israel route, according to multiple sources close to the investigation, amid increasingly difficult questions about the circumstances of the narrowly avoided tragedy.

stories.title: Skull fractures suggest servants of Egypt’s ancient kings were sacrificed
stories.summary: Study of remains taken from royal cemetery at Umm el-Qa’ab appears to confirm early Egyptologist’s theory Court officials and craftspeople serving early Egyptian kings may have been sacrificed when their ruler died, according to research that found fractures in several ancient skulls. The royal cemetery of Umm el-Qa’ab near Abydos features the tombs and enclosures of the First Dynasty rulers of Egypt, and dates as far back as 3,000BC. Continue reading...

stories.summary: Spain’s Socialist prime minister, Pedro Sánchez, has announced a snap general election three days after rightwing parties torpedoed the emergency legislation his minority government had put forward in response to growing public anger over the housing crisis. Sánchez, who has been in office since 2018, announced his decision, which had been widely expected, in a televised address on Monday morning. stories.title: US marine arrested in Japan on suspicion of killing woman, police say

The suspect allegedly “killed [a] 39-year-old woman at a hotel in Naha and stole her wallet” as well as her backpack, local police told news media outlets. Continue reading...

stories.summary: Brazilian President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva and Flávio Bolsonaro have a final chance on Saturday to sway voters at rallies in crucial São Paulo before a tight election marked by scandals and personal attacks.

The game-winning sneakers sold for $2.2 million at Sotheby's in New York on Tuesday, smashing the sneaker auction record of $1.47 million, set in 2021 by a pair of Nike Air Ships that Jordan wore earlier in his career.
